key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures without exhaustive search.
engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable design rules for choosing ETL, absorber, and HTL materials to improve charge extraction, reduce recombination, and accelerate device optimization.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen stacks
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors for performance
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation, and the top candidates were verified with full SCAPS-1D simulations, reaching up to 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: The ML predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so transfer to real devices may still require experimental validation and attention to interface defects and fabrication variability.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
